newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares soar on strong A share rally.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares soar on strong A share rally.

text.p: Shanghai's B share index soared on Friday, propelled by early gains in the domestic currency A share index on a strong showing by Shenzhen-listed Shenzhen Development Bank, brokers said.
The Shanghai B index closed up 1.822 points or 2.19 percent at 1,349.150 points on turnover of 17.304 million shares worth $10.389 million compared with Thursday's $7.892 million.
"The main reason for the gain was the strong performance in the A share market," said one broker. "The Pudong counters also played a role in today's gains."
The A share index skyrocketed 64.136 points to 1,349.150, a rise of 4.99 percent on turnover of 453.65 million shares worth 6.458 billion yuan.
"The Shenzhen Development Bank sparked the Shenzhen A market rally, which then helped the Shanghai A market," the broker said.
Shenzhen's A share index rose 22.54, or 5.35 percent, to 444.14 points in late Friday morning trading due to a strong performance by market leader Shenzhen Development Bank Co, brokers said.
"Rises on the Shenzhen A market boosted the confidence of Shanghai's domestic investors," another broker said.
The bank surged 3.09 points to its 10 percent limit up after ending a five-day trading suspension by Beijing following the sacking of the bank's president for illegal trading.

Chinese securities regulators also confiscated nearly 100 million yuan in profits which the bank had made by speculating in its own shares, and punished a string of listed firms and brokerages for trading irregularities.
Brokers also said the index was pushed up because technical charts showed signs of over-selling after it had lost more than 20 percent since early May due to Beijing's crackdown on the markets.
Brokers said the A and B share markets might see smaller gains early next week.
"With such a big rebound today there might be smaller rises next week but no gains as big as today's," one broker said.
"A new run cannot start without fresh capital inflow but the market will move forward a little if there is no negative news over the weekend."
Pudong-based Shanghai Waigaoqiao Free Trade Zone Development Co Ltd was the day's second-biggest gainer, rising 6.60 percent to $0.614, brokers said.
The biggest B share market loser was textile machine maker Shanghai Erfangji Co Ltd, which lost 4.41 percent to close at $0.130.
Shanghai Jinqiao Export Processing Zone Development Co Ltd, another Pudong counter, rose 4.04 percent to $0.874 on the day's second-heaviest turnover of 2.04 million shares.
The B market's sharpest gainer was Shanghai Vacuum and Electron Device Co Ltd, which soared $0.018, or 9.00 percent, to $0.218.
The rise in the Shanghai A market was led by blue chip companies, including big electronics maker Sichuan Changhong Electric Co, brokers said.
Changhong rose 7.03 percent to 41.10 points.
